name: When should I consider replacing my entire sewer line instead of just repairing a collapsed section?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing my entire sewer line instead of just repairing a collapsed section?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing your entire sewer line if there are multiple collapses, extensive damage along a significant portion of the pipe, or if the pipe material is old and prone to recurring issues. Frequent repairs can be more costly in the long run than a full replacement. Additionally, if the existing sewer line is undersized for your property's needs or is made of outdated materials, a full replacement can offer a more durable and long-term solution. A professional assessment can help determine the most cost-effective and lasting option.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider full replacement for multiple collapses, extensive damage, or if the pipe is old and frequently problematic. This can be more cost-effective than ongoing repairs.
